question: does any public measurement reach enough of the 882 real-unknown blocks to score milestone 1.3's clause 2 (a gene and a tissue per block) at the calibrated sizing?

sizing.source: lane-s2 cab70d9 (registered 019a9ab), calibrated on CRISPRi element-gene readouts

incidental_displays: 2026-10-10, a header peek printed two data rows of ENCFF528RAY (PPIF, hg19) and three of ENCFF149IDL (FADS2, GRCh38), effect-size columns included; a later header check printed one row of ENCFF197SZI (a MYC guide's count). All six intervals lie outside every one of the 882 blocks (checked on the lifted coordinates), and none enters any count

verdict.element_perturbation: Every public element-perturbation screen with a gene readout, pooled, tested an element against a protein-coding gene in 13 of the 882 real-unknown blocks (14 counting the libraries whose gene is not resolved per guide, as an upper bound). The smallest calibrated design needs 75 compared blocks, so the shortfall is 62 blocks to that floor and 518 to the design for a half; it is not met by anything published.
verdict.reporter_and_growth: Reporter assays reach more blocks (encode_lentimpra_joint_library 167, encode_mpra_element_references 385, vista 55, mpravardb 34) and the growth screens encode_cell_growth_screens 153, but neither names a gene, so neither can score the clause's 'attributed to a gene'.
verdict.natural_perturbation: The one source whose tested universe reaches the sizing is GTEx v8 fine-mapped cis-eQTL: 879 of 882 blocks (530 of the 531 carrying a scored element) hold at least one dbSNP common single-nucleotide variant, the proxy used here for a variant GTEx tested. Its endpoint names a gene and a tissue. Its sensitivity rises with a variant's frequency, which purifying selection lowers, so a fair test must match its controls on the variants they carry; the fine-mapped track itself has not been read.

decision.why: Among the sources inventoried here, only CRISPR perturbation names the gene an element was tested against, and it reaches 13 blocks against a coding gene (14 as an upper bound), under the 75 the smallest calibrated design needs. The calibrated sizing (cab70d9) describes that endpoint and no other. The fine-mapped eQTL route reaches 879 blocks by the tested-variant proxy, but its window rate, its clustering and its sensitivity have never been calibrated in this project, and its control has yet to be chosen, so the sizing cannot say it is enough. No test is registered by this lane.
what_the_clause_needs: 62 more blocks with an element tested against a coding gene for the smallest calibrated design, 518 more for the design for a half; no published screen inventoried here supplies them

or, on natural variation: a power calibration of a fine-mapped eQTL arm measured on sequence outside the 882 blocks, a control matched on length, common-variant count and distance to the named gene's start, and a registration, all before the gtexDapg track is read over the blocks
decision.prior_exposure: earlier lanes range-read the gtexDapg track over storage units of the UNKNOWN space (human_panel) and at 1,505 CRISPRi elements (finemap_dapg); whether any of those rows lie in the 882 blocks is not checked here, because checking would read them

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record cfc30e4

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
